historical_transitions.summary: WildcatArchController deployed by EOA 0xb4B9f935bf0189c2FF46165F04b0D517e9553FBc at block 18686645 (2023-11-30): the non-proxy singleton registry that records borrowers, hooks factories and market templates for Wildcat's undercollateralised credit markets. Runtime code 8724 bytes, verified source on Blockscout, owned by Safe 0xC15bE5214978d1fc509ECdd4f9D5BC067C94D9Ae.

Wildcat V2 mainnet expansion: HooksFactory 0xDd7dd3b5076Cf89440d05585FF56d246386207Be deployed at block 21788182 (same-day WildcatMarket initCodeStorage 0xAc3216FA28F81B8FaE150fB5626ca79C7a570DAf at block 21788178, tx 0x2ac9bce6eeabd55459dcc70d4474d3b5cce2dd08cd340a6bd095143fb3727f41). V2 adds hook-templated market behaviour while reusing the immutable V1 ArchController as the registry; no replacement controller was deployed.

ArchController runtime bytecode at the Pacta pinned block 26450616 is byte-identical to block 18686646 (sha256 prefix 4988e6580cf924ab at both heights): no proxy upgrade, selfdestruct or redeploy across 2023-2026. Protocol evolution happened only through new periphery contracts (V2 HooksFactory, MarketLens, sanctions sentinel) wired into the same registry.

evidence_sources.claim_summary: Pre-deploy snapshot of docs.wildcat.finance already shows a 'V1 -> V2 Changelog' nav entry and a notice that the docs 'recently underwent substantial changes to incorporate Wildcat V2 details': web documentation tracked V2 before mainnet launch.
GITBOOK-140 'Duplicating Terms of Use page to adjust V2 app appropriateness' (2025-01-16): V2 documentation edits landed weeks before the 2025-02-06 mainnet deployment.
'Update whitepaper_v2.0.pdf' committed two days after the V2 mainnet deploy, closing the V1-only whitepaper gap that opened at block 21788182.

The v2-protocol README still labels both the whitepaper and the V1 GitBook '[Out Of Date For V2]' (README last touched 2024-08-29), a stale signpost that survives even though the whitepaper itself was updated to v2.0.

gap_windows.summary: Whitepaper v1.0 was the canonical spec when V2 went live at block 21788182; whitepaper_v2.0.pdf was committed 2025-02-08 (block 21801898), a 2-day specification gap. The web docs had no gap: their V1->V2 changelog predates the deployment.

The v2-protocol README still flags the whitepaper and V1 documentation as '[Out Of Date For V2]' ~652 days after the v2.0 whitepaper shipped: a stale-pointer documentation-hygiene gap that can misdirect auditors to a superseded spec.

executive_risk_memo: Wildcat is an undercollateralised credit protocol (~$296M TVL) whose control plane is the WildcatArchController, a non-proxy singleton deployed 2023-11-30 and byte-identical at the 2026-11-19 pinned block (sha256 prefix 4988e6580cf924ab): the registry itself cannot be upgraded in place, which is the strongest possible control-plane posture for the core contract. Risk instead concentrates in three mutable surfaces. First, the ArchController's owner is a Safe (0xC15bE5214978d1fc509ECdd4f9D5BC067C94D9Ae) that can register new hooks factories and market templates, so governance capture of that Safe expands what borrowers can deploy. Second, the 2025-02-06 V2 expansion moved market behaviour into borrower-selected hooks (FixedTermHooks, OpenTermHooks, sanctions sentinel), shifting safety invariants from the core into per-market configuration; lender safety now depends on each borrower's hook choice rather than on protocol-wide enforcement. Third, engineering reality is asymmetric: the contracts repo saw only 6 commits in 12 months against 373 on the V2 frontend, with a bus factor of ~2, so review bandwidth for hook templates is thin. Documentation kept pace with V2 (changelog pre-dated launch; whitepaper v2.0 shipped +2 days), but the README still points auditors to superseded V1 material. Overall: immutable core, mutable periphery, small team; residual risk is configuration and governance capture, not code upgradeability.
